### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **111** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-catalog-refusal.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**51** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-catalog-refusal.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `logError (9 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`
- **33** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **158** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `22453e93735bfcbbd0103a2b841ed922c369a94b` — the merge of head `7b50158db85fc41fb1b6a7c2b77f00be5f857651` into base `394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 22453e93735bfcbbd0103a2b841ed922c369a94b && git checkout 22453e93735bfcbbd0103a2b841ed922c369a94b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520 7b50158db85fc41fb1b6a7c2b77f00be5f857651 && git checkout -B drift-repro 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520 && git merge --no-ff 7b50158db85fc41fb1b6a7c2b77f00be5f857651

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 394f65e891f0ac6c6be708fb807740d5cb446520` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7b50158db85fc41fb1b6a7c2b77f00be5f857651`
Local-runs: none

Served on opus by the maintainer's order 「后续契约复审用 opus就够了」 (seat note 6166448512 on objectstack-ai/objectstack#6367).

This re-reviews PR #23503 (branch `claude/issue-23430-grant-column`) after the pre-PR FAIL record 6166827307 at `c38af85e0e`, as amended by relay 6167238426 and seat answers 6167037655.
- **Net diff:** merge base `0d3ea295d1` (8-post) to head. 47 files, +1,229 / −2,038 = 3,267 changed lines.
- **Face:** `packages/spec/src/**` (the ADR-0087 entry) puts it on the published-schema face. No governed-surface path is touched.
- **Check-runs on this head:** 41 in all: 36 success, 5 skipped, 0 failed.
  - Skipped: Console Pin Gate, the dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, the opt-in tarball smoke, and Temporal Conformance.
  - All five required contexts are success: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard.
  - Test Core runs the cli `integration` project at `OS_TEST_TIERS=queue`, so the ceremony pins ran in CI.

### ① Derived judgments

**Blocking fixes of 6166827307, as amended**

- **Fix 1 (amended to a safety net): discharged.**
  - **Skip and report.** `organization-ownership-grants.ts` `planGrantRewrite` is one decision, taken by both `--plan` and `--apply`.
    - It keys a grant by (user, name, organization), with a NULL organization keyed with NULL.
    - It checks stored named grants and grants named earlier in the same run. That second check also covers two legacy platform-wide grants of one id, which the old `'global'` index allowed.
    - A collision blocks the rewrite. The blocker names both ids, and nothing is deleted.
  - **The `--plan` count.** The plan reports `grants.rewriteCollisions`.
  - **End-to-end pins** in `organization-ownership-apply.test.ts`: the Q-S3b sweep pin and the safety-net pin. Both run on a table carrying `UNIQUE (user_id, permission_set, COALESCE(organization_id, '__global__'))`.
    - That index is the ADR-0120 D3 shape spelled by hand, because the fixture is raw SQLite.
    - The driver's own materialization of it is pinned in plugin-security (Q-S3a below).
    - Reported ablation: with the collision check disabled, the safety-net pin goes red.
  - **The `logReport` wording.** It leads with the ceremony, then the restart. It says that re-granting by name makes a second grant, which the ceremony reports and does not name.
- **Fix 2: withdrawn, and the withdrawal is clean.**
  - `bc150970b5` built the check, and `b3420c9e6e` reverts it exactly: `git diff bc150970b5^ b3420c9e6e` over its two files is empty. Then `32971a8646` retires the door check.
  - On the head, `grant-permission-set-name.ts` differs from the merge base only in comments and in two unused constants that were never on the package entry (`GRANT_SET_ID_FIELD`, `PERMISSION_SET_CATALOG_OBJECT`).
  - No `assertNoPlatformWideDuplicate`, `DuplicateRecordError` or `dispatch.scope` remains in plugin-security source.
  - `plugin-security/package.json` equals both the merge base and current `main`.
  - `pnpm-lock.yaml` equals the merge base; it differs from current `main` only by `main`'s own later change. The `packages/apps/account` churn is gone.
- **Fix 3: discharged.**
  - `dropColumnsThroughDrift` (`organization-ownership-column-drops.ts`) drops the proposed `drop_index` entries for a column's `retiredIndexes` first, in their own `applyMigrationEntries` call, and the `drop_column` follows in a later call. Index names come from `buildIndexName`.
  - An index drop that is skipped fails its column, naming the index, and the column stays.
  - Pinned on a real SqlDriver whose 17.x table carries both legacy indexes:
    - the differ proposes both orphans and the column;
    - the two calls happen in that order;
    - a refused index keeps its column.
  - MySQL's refusal is still a reading of the driver arm, not a run.
- **Fix 4: discharged.**
  - The inventory category is gone: `organization-ownership-inventory.ts` equals `main`.
  - Without the name column, `planGrantKeys` answers `nameColumn: 'absent'`, zero counts, and the "Boot this release once" note.
  - `--apply`'s rewrite then blocks with the `verifyReferences` remedy. Both halves are pinned.
- **Fix 5: discharged.**
  - The dev ran cli `--project integration` on this head: 129 files, 1,125 passed, 2 skipped (6170828501).
  - Test Core (1/6 to 6/6) is green on this head and runs the same tier.

**Q-S3a: the index respelled `unique: 'organization'`**
- **The premise holds.**
  - The object declares no `tenancy`, so `computeTenantField` falls back to the implicit `organization_id`.
  - `normalizeDeclaredIndex` takes the `'organization'` arm with the tenant column already listed (`schema-drift.ts:1864–1866`). The columns stay as listed, and `organization_id` becomes the NULL-safe `COALESCE(organization_id, '__global__')` key part.
- **The real-driver pin** is `grant-permission-set-name.test.ts`, on a real ObjectQL engine over a real SqlDriver, with SecurityPlugin started.
  - A platform-wide duplicate is refused for both an admin and a system writer.
  - **Bypass path 1:** a two-row batch is refused and stores nothing.
  - **Bypass path 2:** a raw knex INSERT beneath the engine is refused with `UNIQUE constraint failed`. That raw refusal directly proves that the tenant field resolved to `organization_id`.
  - A rename update that would make a duplicate is refused.
  - An organization-scoped duplicate is refused.
  - The control lands: two organizations plus platform-wide, two users by batch and by raw SQL, and an edit.
  - The revoke pins are kept for both the scoped and the platform-wide case.
- **The ablation.** Respelling the index `'global'` turned exactly the three platform-wide pins red (reported).
- **The wire shape.** The engine throws `DUPLICATE_RECORD` 409, and `mapDataError` answers 409 `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`. Both are asserted on every refusal case.
- **The restatements.** Four places now name the index as the guard for every writer and write path: the changeset, the ADR-0087 entry's `acceptanceCriteria`, the object note, and the anchor.

**Q-S3b: answer (ii)**
- **The change.** In `reconcileOrgAdminGrant`, after the by-name existence check, a find of `{ user_id, organization_id: orgId, permission_set: null }` with limit 1 runs.
  - Any hit returns `skipped: unnamed_grant_awaits_ceremony` and writes nothing.
  - `backfillOrgAdminGrants` and the `sys_member` hook both go through this function.
  - An unnamed grant in another organization does not hold the pair back (control).
- **The pins:**
  - a stub pin;
  - a real-engine pin in `grant-readers-unnamed-grant.test.ts`;
  - the end-to-end cli pin. There, the real `backfillOrgAdminGrants` writes no row (`granted 0, skipped 1`), `--plan` counts no collision, the rewrite names the grant with `collisions: 0`, and the next sweep writes nothing.
- **The ablation.** It is reported for the stub and real-engine pins. The cli pin reads plugin-security's dist, so that ablation did not reach it. Read directly, it still turns red without the skip: the sweep would write the named grant, and `granted: 0` would fail.

**The `main` merges** (read through `git show --remerge-diff`)
- **`fe84a70e8a`, merging `4e0838d99` (#23399):**
  - `ColumnDropOutcome extends ColumnDrop`, so `not-declared` carries `column`, and the blocker names `table.column`.
  - The apply test now counts the grant column as one more due drop: `{dropped: 2, due: 3, notDeclared: 1}`.
  - The conflict resolutions are minimal.
- **`95898bba18`, merging `0d3ea295d1` (8-post):**
  - `catalog-reference-report.ts` keeps 8-post's `SecurityCatalogEntry` import and its sixth class (position definitions naming an unresolved set). It drops `GRANT_SET_ID_FIELD`, and this PR's `logReport` remedy sits beside the sixth class.
  - The handler-count pin resolves to `toHaveLength(1)`.
  - 8-post's edit to the backfill test stays deleted, with its code.
  - The census was re-measured on the merged tree: 227 → 225.
- Nothing else from these merges conflicts in behaviour.

**Whole-diff re-run of the rest**
- These stand as 6166827307 judged them:
  - the declaration;
  - the three readers lose their id leg;
  - the backfill deletion and the deletion clause;
  - the plugin-auth and dogfood flips.
- No engine reader of the retired column survives in non-test source. The only reads left are the ceremony's raw SQL: `runRewrite`, `verifyReferences` and `planGrantKeys`.
- The PR body lists the cli files outside the claim's literal surface:
  - `organization-ownership-apply.ts` and its test;
  - `organization-ownership-plan.ts`;
  - `organization-ownership-grants.ts` (new);
  - `organization-ownership-column-drops.ts` and its test (new);
  - one line of the served-catalog test.

  It also lists the other files outside it: plugin-auth, the core comment, the dogfood pin, the census, and the engine-double ledger. All are right in scope.

### ② Semver level
- **The level is right.**
  - `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/spec` each take `minor`, marked BREAKING under the launch-window convention.
  - `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` appears in the changeset and on the PR body's line 2.
  - There is exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `registered ups-permission-set-id-column-retired`, in the same changeset body.
  - Check Changeset and Lint & Repo Gates are green.
- **What narrows in plugin-security:**
  - the declaration: a write naming the column is refused 400 `INVALID_FIELD`, meta stops serving the field, and records stop carrying it;
  - the index now refuses a platform-wide duplicate (409) that it used to accept;
  - the boot backfill is gone, with its `sys_migration` entry;
  - the reconcile writes nothing beside an unnamed grant;
  - Leg C now restricts on any unnamed, unscoped human grant.
- **cli:**
  - `--plan` gains a `grants` block, which is additive.
  - `--apply`'s rewrite can now block on a collision.
  - `column-drops` now drops a new column and two indexes.
  - `ColumnDropPort` is not on the package entry.
- **spec:** one additive entry.
- **No changeset is needed for:** plugin-auth (comments and one test), core (one comment), and dogfood (private).
- **The migration text is present:**
  - FROM → TO with a one-line fix for the column, the indexes and the backfill;
  - the 17.x window sentence;
  - the instruction to restart after `--apply`.
- **Optional:** the first FROM → TO bullet could also say that records no longer carry the key.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Size: Tier H by AGENTS §7 (c).**
- 3,267 changed lines (1,229 + 2,038), which is over 3,000.
- It stays a single PR, by the seat's answer to 6169001411's open question 1. The `'organization'` index and the ceremony's collision handling are coupled, so I agree.
- Landing path:
  1. The seat gives its ACCEPT.
  2. The seat posts a final `## 维护者速读` as a COMMENT, because the body's 草稿 does not stand in for it, and adds `needs-user-decision`.

  4. The owning seat lands it.

**`## 维护者速读（草稿）`**
- Present, in Chinese, from the business angle.
- It covers what changes, why, the risks and costs (the 17.x window, 400/409, rollback), and the action. 席位意见 is left empty for the seat. It is accurate.
- One nit: the risk line says 「需人工合并」, while the action line gives the real path (approval, then the seat lands it).

**Open questions and out-of-scope findings in the three reports**
- **6165963520:**
  - OQ1 (the door widened to system writers) and OQ3 (batches) retired with the door under Q-S3a. The index meets every writer and every path, and that is pinned.
  - OQ2 (unnamed grants reached by no reconcile) is accepted, and is now (ii).

- **6169001411:**

  - OQ2 (the safety net's "any other writer"): accepted. Setup, data-door grants and seeds are the in-repo writers left.
  - OQ3 (`tryFind` fails open, so the pair is granted): accepted. The rewrite reports the pair. That costs the operator work; no data is lost.
  - Non-blocking items:

- **6170828501:** no new questions.

**Composition with the sibling PRs**
- **S4 #23437 is on `main` as `f9b421716d`.** It merged at 15:05Z, after this head's checks.
  - It touches four of this PR's files: `organization-ownership.ts`, `organization-ownership-apply.ts`, its test, and the served-catalog test.
  - **Text:** read hunk by hunk, no hunks overlap.
    - S4's `type ReviewedPlan` import lands one unchanged line below this PR's removed `type ColumnDropOutcome`.
    - S4's `reviewedPlan,` lands three lines below this PR's port body.
    - All other hunks are far apart.
  - **Behaviour:**
    - S4 makes `ApplyOptions.reviewedPlan` required. Every new ceremony test here goes through the shared `apply()` helper, which S4 updated.
    - No other user of the column-drop port exists on `main`.
    - The inventory, and so the digest S4 compares, is unchanged.
  - **Not computed:** the PR's `mergeable: clean` still names base `394f65e891`, which predates S4. Under ruling #23390 no merge is owed unless GitHub or the queue reports a conflict or a red.
- **S1 #23452 (seat 2, draft, based on `5656c5638a`)** shares the four ceremony files.
  - **The second lander meets certain textual conflicts:**
    - both PRs add a `TablePlan` field after `templateConflicts` (`metadataConflicts` and `grants`);

  - **Behaviour is independent.** S1's new steps keep `rewrite` before `column-drops`, which this PR's read of the id column needs.
- **S2 #23469 (draft)** shares four things:

  - one line of the apply test near the `answering` case;

  S2's family `organization_id` drops ride this PR's port as plain `{ table, column }`, without `retiredIndexes`. Whether S2's orphaned organization-keyed indexes need the index-first order on MySQL is S2's call (the prior record's "possibly pre-existing" note). This PR's mechanism is the tool for it.
- **S5 #23461 (draft)** shares only `organization-ownership-apply.ts`, where it re-exports `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_MIGRATION_ID` at the file head. No hunks overlap.
  - Its guard reads `organization_id` columns only, never `permission_set_id`. It refuses `os serve` on a 17.x database, which closes this PR's no-grant-confers window.
  - Schema sync runs before its `kernel:ready` throw, so the plan's "Boot this release once" can still be satisfied.
  - S5's body reports its dogfood order pin 4/4 on a scratch merge of S5, S2 and S3.

2. **S3 #23503 next.**
   - Re-read its mergeability against `f9b421716d` before the approval request.

## 维护者速读 · PR #23503（#23430，C7b S3）· `domain:engine` seat 1 · 2026-10-14T15:42Z

**改了什么**
- **下线旧列：** 用户授权表 `sys_user_permission_set` 去掉旧的 `permission_set_id` 列和它的两个索引。授权只按权限集名称引用。
- **唯一键改为** (`user_id`, `permission_set`, `organization_id`)，声明为 `unique: 'organization'`。
  - 组织为空的平台级授权也由数据库索引本身拒绝重复。
  - 拦截覆盖所有写入路径：普通写入、批量写入、并发写入和迁移脚本的原始 SQL。
- **删除启动时的"授权按名补全"模块，** 改由 v18 迁移仪式（`os migrate organization-ownership`）在验证后改写。改写时：
  - 先删旧索引，再删旧列；
  - 撞键的旧授权只报告、不删除；
  - `--plan` 会预先统计这类情况。
- **扫描不再补写：** 用户在某组织已有未命名的旧授权时，组织管理员授权的启动扫描不再在旁边另写一条，避免迁移时撞键。

**为什么改**
- 依据 ADR-0131 D4/D10：授权只按名称引用权限集。旧 id 列要等每条授权都有名称后才能删除，这是 #15211 的第 S3 阶段。
- 旧唯一索引按 id 建，而按名写入的授权该列为空，所以它从未拦住过重复授权。
- 重复授权的后果是：撤销其中一条后，另一条仍然生效。

  - 没有 S5 时，本 PR 是"失败即关闭"：权限变少，不会变多。
- **接口变化：**
  - 带 `permission_set_id` 写授权的种子数据或调用，会收到 `400 INVALID_FIELD`；
  - 重复授权会收到 `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION`。
